transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-24
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jon (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood Solutions), Carlos (SummitPay CTO), Priya (SummitPay Head of ML), Evelyn (SummitPay Infra)

Summary (auto): Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize features focused on batching and caching (prefix/KV cache). Cost modeling examples and next-step to run short benchmark using customer traces.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this tight \u0014 40ish minutes \u0014 walk through Optimize recommendations for batching and kv/prefix cache and then leave time for q's. can you hear me ok?
[00:08] Carlos: yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya. excited to see the numbers \u0014 Priya and Evelyn are on for the infra and model parts.
[00:14] Priya: yep thanks, we're mostly interested in latency under concurrent traffic and how kv cache hit rate helps costs.
[00:22] Jon: cool, i'll share my screen in a sec, but quick agenda: batching basics, continuous batching, prefix vs kv cache, cost model example (1M tokens baseline), and suggested configs for a payments chat use case.
[00:34] Maya: quick note, we also included a link to the benchmark sheet in the calendar \u0014 i'll drop it in chat after.

[02:10] Jon: okay first, batching tradeoffs \u0014 larger batch sizes improve GPU amortization but can add queuing latency; we typically pick a target 95th-percentile latency SLO and tune batching window to meet that. for example with gpus we'll aim for batch sizes of 8-32 depending on sequence length. audio: uh hmm
[02:30] Priya: sequence length for our chat is usually 80-220 tokens \u0014 lots of short interactions but occasional long histories.
[02:38] Jon: that distribution is helpful \u0014 for mixed short + long, we recommend adaptive batching where short requests are prioritized and long ones go in a separate lane, or use quick prefix caching to avoid re-encoding prefixes.
[02:50] Evelyn: when you say prefix cache, is that the same as the kv cache i've heard about? sometimes the docs overlap.
[02:57] Jon: great question, slight dif: prefix caching stores repeated token prefixes at the request level (like repeated system prompts), kv cache is the attention key/value cache across steps for a single conversation which saves recomputation of past tokens. both reduce compute but behave differently on hit patterns.

[04:20] Maya: and in Optimize you'll see hit-rate projections given a token distribution \u0014 we built a simple model that converts hit-rate to cost saving and latency improvement.
[04:35] Carlos: can you show the cost model example? numbers are what leadership wants.
[04:40] Jon: sure \u0014 i'll pull up the example sheet. note the numbers are illustrative but match recent benchmarks. baseline: hosted gen model at 8-bit quantized runtime costs approx $0.15 per 1k output tokens (this is illustrative), with batching and a 40% kv hit-rate cost drops to ~ $0.09 per 1k because you avoid re-decoding prefixes.
[05:12] Priya: 40% hit-rate \u0014 that's realistic for us? we reuse system prompts but user context varies.
[05:20] Jon: depends \u0014 for payment confirmation flows where the system prompt and intent are stable you'll see high prefix reuse; conversational histories lower. we can model your traces to compute an expected hit-rate \u0014 that's the benchmark step.

[07:00] Jon: also important: latency SLO interplay. if you increase batch windows to raise throughput you can push p95 from 120ms to 210ms. some teams accept that for throughput cost-savings; others prefer dedicated and lower batch windows for stable low p95.
[07:18] Evelyn: on dedicated \u0014 what are lock-in or data isolation guarantees? we need VPC + KMS.
[07:25] Maya: dedicated gives reserved GPU pools in your region, private control plane option, and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management \u0014 we'll attach the security pack and SOC2/ISO docs in the follow-up.

[09:05] Carlos: curious about fallback behavior \u0014 if KV cache miss spikes, do requests fall back to a cheaper model or to hosted?
[09:14] Jon: yes, Optimize supports smart routing: when capacity constraints hit or hit-rate drops we'll route to compatible model variants or dedicated bursts. you can set automatic fallbacks and per-route policies. note fallbacks change cost and often increase latency.

[11:30] Jon: demo snippet: here's a synthetic workload with 1k rps and 60% short requests; with continuous batching and a 35% kv hit-rate we saw 3.6x token/sec throughput improvement and 48% cost reduction vs naive single-request runs. transcribe note: numbers approximate
[11:52] Priya: what's the overhead for maintaining KV cache across many conversations? memory concerns?
[12:00] Jon: great \u0014 KV cache size is proportional to sequence length and number of concurrent conversations pinned in memory. Optimize offers TTL and LRU eviction policies, plus a cache tiering option \u0014 small hot cache on GPU, larger on shared RAM backed storage. eviction config typically solves memory pressure.
[12:20] Evelyn: any extra operational complexity? we want minimal changes to our current infra.
[12:26] Jon: minimal \u0014 API stays the same. you'll pass conversation IDs to maintain KV state across turns; Optimize handles cache lifecycle. for private deployments we provide a control plane that integrates with your logging and tracing.

[14:40] Maya: quick pause \u0014 i'm going to jump to an example cost table. if you look at scenario A (no caching), monthly cost projected $24k for 1M monthly active chats; scenario B (40% kv hit) drops to $13k; scenario C with prefix caching + batching tuned for your token distribution drops further to ~ $9.5k. the sheet shows assumptions about average output length and request distribution.
[15:15] Carlos: ok leadership will like that. are those numbers after quantization?
[15:19] Jon: yes they assume 8-bit quantized kernels where supported; we also show a delta if you run in fp16 for slightly better latency but higher cost.
[15:30] Priya: any impacts on model quality from quantization? we've seen noise with aggressive quant.
[15:35] Jon: small changes for some sensitive prompts; Optimize recommends evaluating quality regression tied to a prompt set. we can run evals on your prompts during the POC and track metrics.

[17:10] Maya: checklist for the POC we proposed: 1) customer shares sample traffic (token histograms + 48h traces), 2) we'll run a 48h benchmark with hosted dev cluster and identical load, 3) SE will produce cost/latency projections + recommended batching/cache config, 4) if results look good we scope Dedicated.
[17:40] Priya: that sounds good. we can provide traces but will need to mask PII \u0014 is there guidance?
[17:48] Maya: yes we have a tracing sanitizer script and a secure upload link; i'll include the steps in the follow-up.

[19:05] Carlos: question on telemetry \u0014 will we get token-level cost breakdowns per route?
[19:12] Jon: yes Redwood Console shows per-route token breakdown, cost by model, p95/p99 latency, and per-token emitter details. you can export CSVs to plug into your internal finance dashboards.

[21:00] Evelyn: what about multi-region routing? we have users in EU and NA and need data residency options.
[21:07] Maya: we support region routing and private deployments with customer-controlled regions; for strict residency we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated in the specific region.

[23:30] Priya: ok, curious about one more optimization \u0014 delta caching across similar prompts (like templated confirmations). do you do semantic dedupe?
[23:40] Jon: we do some fingerprinting for templated prefixes; semantic dedupe is trickier but we can approximate with shingled hashes or embeddings-based grouping. it's part of an advanced config and we can discuss as an enhancement during the POC.

[26:00] Carlos: are there any known gotchas for payments workloads? like sensitive token leakage with caches?
[26:08] Jon: security-first: caches are tenant-isolated; for sensitive fields we recommend client-side redaction or tokenization before sending. we also support per-route encryption for cached blobs when using Dedicated/Private.

[28:15] Maya: i just dropped the benchmark sheet and docs link in chat (redwood.com/docs/optimize and the sample csv).
[28:25] Priya: got it.

[30:10] Jon: final notes on tuning: start conservative with small batch windows to protect p95, enable kv/prefix cache for stable prefixes, iterate on TTLs and eviction once you have hit-rate numbers. our cost model will take your histogram and produce a projected saving band (low/median/high).

[33:02] Carlos: ok we want the 48h benchmark. what's the lead time?
[33:07] Jon: if you provide traces by Friday we can run the benchmark over the weekend and have results early next week \u0014 say Monday/Tuesday.

[33:15] Maya: i'll follow up with the security pack and the upload link today.

[35:40] Priya: one operational question \u0014 when KV cache is warmed for a user, do you pin it indefinitely? we have long-lived sessions sometimes.

[35:48] Jon: default TTL is 24 hours but configurable; you can pin sessions for premium users or evict aggressively for anonymous traffic.

[37:10] Evelyn: last Q: pricing for Dedicated commit tiers?

[37:15] Maya: i'll include the reserved capacity tiers in the pricing sheet; we have monthly and annual commit discounts plus optional burst capacity.

[39:05] Maya: ok i think that's it, thanks everyone. recap of next steps in chat: Jon runs benchmark, Maya sends pricing/security, Priya shares traces. we'll schedule a POC kickoff next week.

[39:22] Carlos: great thanks all.

[39:25] Priya: thanks, talk soon.

[39:30] Jon: thanks everyone.

End of transcript. Possible transcription artifacts: speaker labels sometimes generic, occasional misheard words (e.g., kv vs k-v), numbers rounded.
